results.reasoning: Omron's fleet controller is its own Fleet Operations Workspace (FLOW) Core; the release notes' compatibility matrix lists only Omron hardware (Lynx, LD-60/90/CT, LD-250, HD-1500, EM2100), and the command interface is Omron's own ARCL (Advanced Robotics Command Language) — see wireless guide pp.41-42 'ARCL Server' / 'Outgoing ARCL Connection' and release-notes pp.3-4 ARCL command list. Note the tension with the multi_fleet_capable verdict below: Omron sells a Unified Fleet License for multi-vendor AMRs, but that is still Omron's proprietary controller managing foreign robots, not an open/standard controller.

systematic_patterns.title: This dossier is mostly a coverage gap, not a value conflict — and the diff over-counts it
systematic_patterns.detail: 18 of 22 items are 'sonnet null vs opus value' (opus simply extracted company-level fields that sonnet never attempted), 2 are pure serialisation differences, and only 2 are genuine head-to-head value conflicts. Worse, at least one 'disagreement' is a placement artefact: Omron max_fleet_size = 100 WAS extracted by sonnet, just staged on three product rows instead of in company_wide_context. A CWC-block-only diff cannot see per-product placement and will keep manufacturing phantom disagreements. Recommendation: future diffs for company-wide fields should union the CWC block with the per-product fields before comparing.

systematic_patterns.title: Both concessions have the same root cause: a document that is not making a product claim
systematic_patterns.detail: ek robotics cleanroom_class came from a tick-box in a blank RFQ intake form — ek robotics asking the CUSTOMER whether their site is a cleanroom. DS Automotion 'WMS' came from a paragraph whose actual point is that NAVIOS REPLACES a separate warehouse-management system ('alles innerhalb einer Software'). Neither is the vendor asserting a capability. Proposed rule for company_wide_context: a value may only be staged if it is an assertion the vendor makes about its own product. Questions posed to the buyer, and functions described as substituting for the buyer's system, are not assertions of capability.

systematic_patterns.title: The two concessions are both COND_KO fields — errors clustered exactly where they cost most
systematic_patterns.detail: Of 22 items, only 4 are COND_KO-level (infrastructure_free, cleanroom_class, both integration_capability entries). Both concessions and one of the two revisions sit in that group of 4. The confirmations cluster in CONTEXT/SCORING fields. Company-wide extraction is therefore accurate where it does not matter and unreliable where it does — argues for mandatory human review of COND_KO fields in any CWC block, and for treating CONTEXT-level CWC fills as low-risk bulk.

systematic_patterns.title: New failure mode versus the product-field round: correct values carried by broken citations
systematic_patterns.detail: Three items are right for the wrong reason, which a naive spot-check would misjudge. (a) Omron max_fleet_size: opus quoted a footnote 'Contact your local OMRON representative for fleets larger than 100' that does not exist in i828 or i885 — the real *1 footnote is about licence expiration; the value is nonetheless printed on p.1 of both datasheets. (b) Omron multi_fleet_capable: opus argued from a compatibility matrix listing only Omron's own models, which proves nothing about other vendors; the value survives solely on the i828 p.3 'Unified Fleet License … among multi-vendor AMRs' row that neither pass cited. (c) DS modification_process: opus cited a weak p.7 line about runtime parameters and hedged, while the decisive sentence naming the Anlagenbetreiber as the actor sits in the p.10 FAQ. In all three cases a reviewer following the stated citation would have rejected a true value. Citation quality needs to be audited separately from value correctness.

systematic_patterns.title: Company-wide blocks inherit an entity-identity problem that per-product extraction never hits
systematic_patterns.detail: KNAPP's only address belongs to 'KNAPP Industry Solutions GmbH'; the string 'KNAPP AG' appears nowhere in the 34-page folder. Opus flagged the mismatch and then wrote hq_city into the KNAPP AG record anyway. Geography and certification fields are entity-specific by definition, so an unresolved company-identity flag should HARD-BLOCK company-level fills, not merely annotate them. (ek robotics has the same open question — 'a NEURA brand', legal entity NEURA Mobile Robots GmbH — but the disputed ek fields are all product-capability fields, so the identity question does not bind there.)

systematic_patterns.title: AP0 structural finding: reference_count lives on Product but the only available data is company-level
systematic_patterns.detail: Both KNAPP (150) and ek robotics (400) hit this. The figure is a company installed-base claim, but AP0 stores reference_count on the Product entity, so it is written identically to 5 and 7 product rows respectively and inflates aggregate maturity scoring. This is not an extraction error and will recur on every supplier — worth a Tech Lead ruling on whether reference_count should be company-scoped or explicitly documented as 'company figure repeated per product'.

systematic_patterns.title: Serialisation: sonnet emits scalars for AP0 Multi-Select fields
systematic_patterns.detail: installation_process and modification_process are data_type 'Multi-Select' in config/fields.json; sonnet wrote bare strings ('Client', 'Client: All'), opus wrote lists. 2 of the 22 'disagreements' are nothing but this. Any import script must coerce scalar → single-element list for Multi-Select fields, and the diff tool should normalise before comparing so these stop consuming review attention.
